text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PD#789012 triggered — metric: inference-serving.latency.p99 > 1.5s in us-west-2 for model-redwood/v2. Route: hosted-api-prod. Threshold breach count: 3. Link: https://pagerduty.example/pd/789012 :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident created: PD-789012 — https://pagerduty.example/incidents/789012

sam: Ack'd. I'm on it. assigning to myself. :hand:

sam: Checking dashboards, looks like a short spike from a single proxy cluster. p99 jumped to 1.6s around 12:34 UTC, then another blip at 12:35.

maya: Are customers impacted? any 500s?

sam: No 5xx. Error rates steady. It's latency only. Quick snip of logs:
```
2026-03-17T12:34:21Z proxy-12 cpu=68% route=hosted-api p99=1600ms
2026-03-17T12:35:05Z proxy-13 cpu=72% p99=1580ms
```

maya: Looks like synthetic canary run overlapped with autoscaler scale-up, causing temporary queuing on proxy. I bumped canary to run less frequently in prod now.

sam: I applied suppression for duplicate PD pages for 5m, and set route fallback to model-redwood/v2-quant on overflow as a protective measure (runbook step 3).

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-789012 auto-resolved (condition cleared).

sam: Confirming clearing on metrics — p99 back to 350ms. No customer complaints in SLO channel.

leo: I'll take watch for 30m in case it reappears. Leaving notes on incident doc: https://wiki.example/incident/PD-789012

maya: Filing brief postmortem note — suspected cause: canary timing + transient autoscaler lag. Will adjust canary schedule and add longer pre-warm to autoscaler in next sprint. :memo:

sam: Handoff to @leo. Marking resolved. If it comes back re-open PD and escalate to infra.
